/ AWAR D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that vide notification bearing No.
F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, the Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

sentences.text: The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi, was acquired.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioner is the interested person and is owner/bhumidhar in actual and physical possession of share of the land bearing Khasra no. 46/10 total land admeasuring 1 bigha (in short the said land) situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi.

5. It is stated that the petitioner has received the compensation amount of Rs. 7,46,043 on 12.05.2017 in respect of the said land, however, the petitioner came to know that the actual cost of land as on 12.05.2017 was fixed by ld. LAC @ Rs. 5,15,966.76 per bigha, therefore, the present petition has been filed.
LAC no. 11/2018 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sunil Kumar Jain v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 11 6.

entities.text: Sunil Kumar Jain v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is stated that the petitioner is entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.

The actual physical possession of the said land is with the petitioner as the physical possession of the land has not been taken, and the respondents shall take possession thereof from the petitioner.

The LAC failed to take note of the actual and practical market value and had adopted a narrow approach while observing that no proof to claim market value of the said land more than rate fixed by LAC has been filed.
The LAC has not assessed the actual market value of the said land in spite having knowledge of the fair market value of the adjoining land, adjudicated by the courts.

The LAC has failed to properly appreciate the quality,
status, potentiality and development of the said land and its surroundings.

The ld. Counsel for the petitioner has taken the following grounds :
(i) It is stated that the said land is well connected with NH10, Delhi Rohtak Road and Main Karala Mundka Road and the said land is surrounded by many prestigious colonies/village/industries area and the price of each and every commodity has been on rise on day to day basis.

(ii) The said land has potential value as the said land is surrounded by villages like Mundka, Ghevra, Kanjhawala, Nangloi, Karala, mubarakpur and the value in the abovesaid area is not less than Rs. 5,000/ per square yards.

sentences.text: The said land is situated on the main road and very close to PVC Market Tikri, Indian bottling plant, Ghaevra, Chara Mandi Tikri, Netaji Subhash Tourism Centre, proposed Sports Academy at Ghevra, Metro Workshop Mundka and thousands of industries working at the time of notification in the surrounding areas.
It is stated that Sir Chhotu Ram Polytechnic, Kanjhawala and Sir Chhotu Ram High School and Haryana Shakti High School are at a stone thrown distance from the said land.

(iv) It is stated that many developed colonies exists in the surrounding areas i.e. Prem Nagar, Rama Vihar, Agar, Pratap Vihar, Bhagya Vihar which are just adjacent to the said land and which have higher market value i.e. @ Rs. 5,000/ per sq. yards.

The said land has all the necessary facilities i.e.
telephone, electricity, water connection, public school, Govt. School and most frequently served by DTC, Railway Station and other transports.

(v) It is submitted that the ld. LAC has not legally assessed the market value of the said land and has wholly relied upon the policy announcement which came into effect from the financial year 2001 2002, wherein the Government fixed the indicative prices of agricultural land @ Rs. 15.70 lakhs per acre for the acquisition of the agricultural land w.e.f. 01.04.2001, however, this is not the market value of the said land and the ld.
LAC had not considered the fact that the market value had increased between 01.04.2001 to 06.02.2003.
LAC no. 11/2018 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sunil Kumar Jain v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 11 (vi)

sentences.text:
It is stated that the land of the petitioner is fertile and fit for all purposes i.e. commercial,
residential industrial etc. and all facilities and necessities are there and the said land is levelled more than two feet high from the nearby land.
The ld. LAC has not made any efforts to find out the market value of the said land.

There are many sale deeds which shows that the market value of the said land in the surrounding areas adjacent to the said land is very high and the ld. LAC has not considered the said sale deeds dated 05.08.2003, 20.09.2000 and 08.08.2003 of land situated in Village Ghevra and in Savda.

(vii) It is stated that the ld. LAC has never served any notice on the petitioner under Section 12(2) of the Act, in respect of the passing of the announcement of Award, and when the DDA demolished some property in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, it come to the knowledge of petitioner regarding acquisition of the said land.

(viii) By way of the present petition the petitioner sought an increase of Rs. 5,000/ per sq. yards along with 30% solatium on the market value and additional amount under Section 23 (10A) of the Act, along with interest.

OPP 2. Relief.
Counsel for the petitioner as well as ld.
Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 390 of 2016 Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India.

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
12. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.
My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF SO, TO WHAT AMOUNT ? OPP 13.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.

It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC Sh. Sunil Kumar Jain vs Union Of India on 10 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69908133/
4 is always upon the petitioner.

entities.text: Sunil Kumar Jain vs Union Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by LAC no. 11/2018 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sunil Kumar Jain v. Union of India Page no. 8 of 11 our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
14.

sentences.text: To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
15. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

16. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.
LAC no. 11/2018 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sunil Kumar Jain v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 11 17.

sentences.text: In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
18. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
RELIEF 19.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioner is granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.
